syllabusTopics: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tables, theorems based on set operations
Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value
Function: domain and range of a function, inverse function, composite function; algebraic (linear, quadratic and cubic) and transcendental (trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) functions

Curve sketching: odd and even functions, periodicity, symmetry (about origin, X- and Y-axis), monotonicity; graphs of quadratic, cubic and rational functions, trigonometric (asinbx and acosbx), exponential (e^x), logarithmic (lnx)
Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences and series and their properties; A.M, G.M, H.M and their relations; sum of infinite geometric series
Matrices and determinants: transpose of a matrix and its properties; minors and cofactors, adjoint, inverse matrix, determinant, properties of determinants (without proof)
Quadratic equation: nature and roots of a quadratic equation, relation between roots and coefficient, formation of a quadratic equation, symmetric roots, one or both roots common
Complex number: imaginary unit, algebra of complex numbers, geometric representation, absolute (modulus) value and conjugate of complex numbers and their properties, square root of a complex number

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The algebraic-function zoo sorts by rule. **Linear** f = mx + c: slope m is the constant rate (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a); perpendicular slopes multiply to −1. **Quadratic** ax² + bx + c: completing the square yields a(x − h)² + k with **vertex (h, k), h = −b/2a** — minimum for a > 0, maximum for a < 0 (2x² − 8x + 5 → vertex (2, −3), minimum −3).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - slope m = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a); m⊥ = −1/m - ax² + bx + c = a(x − b/2a)² + (c − b²/4a); vertex (−b/2a, c − b²/4a) - rational asymptotes: deg p < deg q ⟹ y = 0; equal ⟹ y = aₚ/b_q; deg p = deg q + 1 ⟹ slant

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Vertex at (-b/2a, f(-b/2a)); minimum for a > 0, maximum for a < 0; vertical asymptotes at zeros of the denominator."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The squaring trap*** — 2sqrt(x+1) = x - 3 demands x >= 3 before squaring; the negative candidate 5 - 2sqrt5 is extraneous, caught only by the sign filter.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Function Zoo, Classified This topic catalogues the algebraic functions — **linear, quadratic, polynomial, rational, composite** — and the graph-reading theorems attached to each: slope as rate, vertex as extremum, asymptotes as forbidden lines.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Linear functions - **f(x) = mx + c**: graph a line; **m = slope = rate of change** = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) — constant for lines. m > 0 rising, m < 0 falling, m = 0 constant. - **Two-point theorem:** a line is determined by two points; parallel lines share slope, perpendicular lines multiply slopes to **−1**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Vertex: -b/2a then substitute. Factor quadratics: two numbers with product c and sum b. Rational asymptotes: compare degrees. Radical equations: square then filter by sign.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. (2m)** — **Factoring route:** seek two numbers with product 6 and sum −5: they are −2 and −3, so x² − 5x + 6 = **(x − 2)(x − 3)**. A product is zero iff a factor is zero: x − 2 = 0 or x − 3 = 0 ⟹ **x = 2 or x = 3**. **Verification:** x = 2: 4 − 10 + 6 = 0 ✓; x = 3: 9 − 15 + 6 = 0 ✓.…  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): Solve for x: 2√(x + 1) = x − 3. (3m)** — **Step 1 — sign condition:** the left side 2√(x+1) is non-negative, so any solution must satisfy **x − 3 ≥ 0, i.e. x ≥ 3** — stated *before* squaring. **Step 2 — square:** 4(x + 1) = (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9 ⟹ x² − 10x + 5 = 0.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For radical equations, state the sign condition before squaring and test both candidates after - the filter is where the marks live.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Completing the square is the quadratic's X-ray: one rewrite exposes vertex, axis, and extremum simultaneously.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Linear f(x) = mx + c: slope = rate of change = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a), constant; parallel = equal slopes; perpendicular slopes multiply to -1. Quadratic f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c: complete the square a(x - h)^2 + k with h = -b/2a; vertex (h, k); minimum if a > 0, maximum if a < 0; axis x = h.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Projectile height is a quadratic in time: the vertex is the peak of the trajectory - the extremum theorem in the open air.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Find the vertex, axis of symmetry and extreme value of f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 5.** — **Vertex x-coordinate:** h = −b/2a = −(−8)/(2·2) = **2**. **Vertex y-coordinate:** k = f(2) = 2(4) − 16 + 5 = **−3**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Slope** | Rate of change (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a) | constant for lines | | **Vertex** | Parabola's extremum at h = −b/2a | minimum if a > 0 | | **Vertical asymptote** | Line x = a where q(a) = 0 | x = 2 for 1/(x−2) | | **Slant asymptote** | Oblique line for deg p = deg q + 1 | x + 1 for (x²+1)/x |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Slope as the universal rate - For any function the difference quotient (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) measures average rate; for lines it is constant — that constancy *is* linearity, and calculus will generalise it.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Rational-function asymptote rules** | Degree relation | Horizontal behaviour | |---|---| | deg p < deg q | y = 0 | | deg p = deg q | y = (leading coefficients ratio) | | deg p = deg q + 1 | slant asymptote (by division) | | deg p > deg q + 1 | no straight asymptote |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Vertex x-coordinate is −b/2a:** not b/2a — the minus sign survives from completing the square.  ·  **Holes vs asymptotes:** a common factor (x − 2)/(x − 2) leaves a **hole** at x = 2; an unfactorable zero of q gives an asymptote.  ·  **Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1:** not "reciprocal" — the reciprocal alone gives parallel-looking errors.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. (2m)** — **Factor:** x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) — two numbers multiplying to 6 and adding to −5 are −2, −3.…  ·  **NEB 2023 (verified PYQ): Solve 2√(x + 1) = x − 3. (3m)** — **Isolate and square:** 2√(x+1) = x − 3 requires x − 3 ≥ 0 (the right side must be non-negative since the left is). Squaring: 4(x + 1) = x² − 6x + 9 ⟹ x² − 10x + 5 = 0 ⟹ x = (10 ± √(100 − 20))/2 = 5 ± 2√5.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Find the vertex and extremum of f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 5.** — h = −b/2a = 8/4 = **2**; k = f(2) = 8 − 16 + 5 = **−3**. Vertex **(2, −3)**; since a = 2 > 0 the parabola opens up and **−3 is the minimum value**, attained at x = 2. Axis of symmetry x = 2.
